title: What do the male sex organs do?
intro: The male sex organs produce sperm and sex hormones and deliver sperm during sex. They include the testicles, a system of ducts, glands and the penis. Understanding them helps people recognise problems and look after their sexual and reproductive health.

sections.heading: The testicles
paragraphs: The two testicles, held in the scrotum outside the body so that they stay slightly cooler than body temperature, produce sperm and the hormone testosterone. Sperm production takes about two to three months. Testosterone drives puberty, muscle growth, voice change, body hair and sex drive.

sections.heading: Ducts and glands
paragraphs: Sperm mature in the epididymis, a coiled tube on each testicle, and travel through the vas deferens, which is cut in a vasectomy. The seminal vesicles and prostate gland add fluids that nourish sperm and form semen. The urethra carries semen and also urine, though not at the same time.

sections.heading: The penis and erection
paragraphs: The penis contains spongy erectile tissue. With arousal, blood flow increases and the tissue fills, making an erection possible. At ejaculation, muscles propel semen out through the urethra. The foreskin covers the head of the penis in uncircumcised males. Nerves, blood vessels, hormones and emotions all affect erections.

sections.heading: Common problems
paragraphs: Problems include infections, erectile difficulties, prostate enlargement, undescended testicles in children, testicular torsion which is an emergency with sudden severe pain, low fertility and cancer. Men should know what is normal for them and seek advice about lumps, swelling, pain or discharge.

sections.heading: Looking after health
paragraphs: Safe sex, vaccination against hepatitis B and human papillomavirus, avoiding smoking and excess alcohol, regular exercise and healthy weight support sexual health. Do not ignore symptoms out of embarrassment. Doctors treat these problems regularly, and many are easy to manage.

examples.title: Noticing a change
examples.text: Imagine you feel a hard lump in a testicle. You could see a doctor soon rather than waiting, since early assessment matters.

examples.title: Protecting health
examples.text: Suppose you have a new partner. You might use condoms and ask about screening for sexually transmitted infections.
